findings.subject: subject-target, responsibilities, and cause-effect
findings.detail: The Japanese draft preserves the Application Log as the subject and preserves the stated artifact boundary, production and Writer uncertainty, deletion consequence, storage priority, write-failure isolation, observability responsibility, and canonical-safety override relationship without changing the responsible target or causal direction.

findings.subject: conditions, prohibitions, obligations, exceptions, and failure/recovery
findings.detail: Daily rotation at the Asia/Tokyo date boundary, date-unit manageability, prohibited recorded information, isolated-write-failure behavior, the canonical-safety exception, Storage Fail Closed applicability, and environment separation obligations are preserved with equivalent modality and scope.

findings.subject: enumeration, unresolved status, additions, deletions, and reordering
findings.detail: The six prohibited-information items and seven unresolved implementation choices are retained in corresponding order and scope. Retention, durability, identifying information, partition/path, additional prohibited-or-masked information, and implementation details remain explicitly unresolved; no semantic item is added or deleted.

findings.subject: first-use explanations and semantic-risk terms
findings.detail: Runtime, Job, Adapter, and Error receive faithful loanword correspondences without narrowing their technical scope, and their later uses preserve the intended concepts.

findings.subject: unredacted redaction and masking meaning
findings.detail: The Japanese wording for unredacted explicitly denotes the absence of masking or concealment and therefore preserves the redaction/masking-specific prohibition rather than generalizing it to merely unedited content.

findings.subject: extra sentence-boundary signal
findings.detail: The additional sentence-boundary signal only marks a natural Japanese sentence division within already corresponding content. It does not assert a new proposition, condition, responsibility, causal relation, obligation, prohibition, exception, or recovery behavior, so it adds no semantic meaning.
